title: Row Subheadings

illustrates.quote: The first column consists of the row headings, which may or may not have a column heading. a. Use 1-3 margins for row headings. b. When there are row subheadings, use 1-5 margins for the primary row headings and 3-5 margins for the secondary row headings. ... (See Sample 11-3: Row Subheadings on page 11-27.)

print.notes: "Machining Centers" and "Punching and Shearing Machines" are primary row headings with no column entries of their own (they head a group); "Production"/"Exports"/"Imports" beneath each are secondary row (sub)headings with their own entries.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box with a heavy rule under the header row; "Item", "1980", "1981" and the two group headings ("Machining Centers", "Punching and Shearing Machines") are bold; the sub-row items (Production/Exports/Imports) are indented and plain.

braille.notes: Line 1 = placeholder "text" for preceding body prose. Primary row headings ",ma*9+ ,c5t]s" (Machining Centers) and ",pun*+ & ,%e>+ ,ma*9es" (Punching and Shearing Machines) begin at the 1-5 margin (cell 1) with no guide dots/entries; the secondary row headings ",produc;n"/",exports"/",imports" are indented to the 3-5 margin, each followed by dot-5 guide dots then their two numeric entries.
